ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart robot that can do lots of things, like play games or answer questions. But, even the people who made this robot, they don't fully understand how it works, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?)

It's like building a really complex Lego castle, but you don't know how all the pieces fit together, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators can make the castle look really cool and work well, but they can't explain exactly how it's doing it, nan desu ka? (what is it?)

This is because the robot uses something called "black box" algorithms, which are like magic spells that make the robot work, tsukamu (do). These algorithms are so complex that even the people who made them can't fully understand how they work, nan desu ka? (what is it?)

It's like trying to explain a dream to someone, but you can't quite put it into words, omoi o tsukamu (in your mind). The creators can show you the robot doing things, but they can't explain the underlying magic, nan desu ka? (what is it?)

So, even though the creators of these robots are really smart, they don't fully understand how they work, kono wa nan desu ka? (what is this?) And that's why they're still learning and trying to figure it out, tsukamu (do).
